messages.author: 56f89e4e966f65cf
messages.subject: Re: how to install brew
parts:
when you installed it, did you specified the lib path?
Go to RApacheinfo page, and look for the libPath.
Then go and view this path, to see if there is the "brew" package.

R often install packages into some place other than
"/usr/lib/R/library" or "/usr/local/lib/R/library/",
while rApache look for packages in these path.

messages.author: 56f89e4e966f65cf
messages.subject: Re: how to install brew
parts:
Put these lines in you apache config file (apache2.conf or other)

<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

then you should be able to go to the info page via:

localhost/RApacheinfo (or your web address)

then find out if brew is in "installed packages" or "attached packages";
also, check the .libPath() to see if the path is the same as where you
install brew in.

I'm also a new for only several days. Get helps and help other... This
is what www be.

messages.author: 56f89e4e966f65cf
messages.subject: Re: how to install brew
parts:
>sudo gedit /etc/apache2/sites-enable/mysite
add these lines (path need to modify) into you site-config file: (here
is 'mysite'. I think you can also add it to apache2.conf)

ScriptAlias /brew/ /home/lan/www/brew/
<Directory "/home/lan/www/brew">
SetHandler r-script
RHandler brew::brew
DefaultType text/html
</Directory>

The first line is to tell your web-script where is folder 'brew' (I
think you know this...)

the others tell apache how to deal with files in folder '....../brew'.

after you add this and restart your server, you could put a test file
'test.brew' in the folder above, with these content:

<%
x<-1:10
print(x)
%>

Now you can access this script via: <your.site.address>/brew/test.brew.
